Parent, Mon: Hi, I noticed Jake's late assignment on the portal is marked as a zero, can that be updated once he turns it in?
Teacher, Mon: Hi! Yes, per the late work policy he can still get up to 80% credit if submitted within a week.
Parent, Wed: It's been two days and I don't see any update, is there a delay on your end?
Teacher, Wed: I haven't received the assignment yet, that's why the grade hasn't changed.
Parent, Wed (later): That's strange, he told me he turned it in. This is honestly getting frustrating, this isn't the first time something has 'gone missing' with your grading. I'd like this looked into today.
Teacher, Wed (later): I understand the frustration. I've checked both the portal and my email and don't see a submission from Jake. I'm happy to have him resubmit in class tomorrow and I'll date-stamp it in front of him so there's no ambiguity going forward.
Parent, Thu: Jake resubmitted this morning and said you stamped it in front of him, thank you for that. For what it's worth, I think what actually happened is he saved it as a draft in the online doc but never hit the final submit button, so from his side it looked done. Sorry for jumping to conclusions about the grading before we'd actually figured out what happened.
Teacher, Thu: No apology needed at all, I'd rather a parent flag a grade concern than let it sit. That explanation makes a lot of sense actually, I've seen that exact draft-vs-submit mix-up trip up a few students this year with the new portal, might be worth a class-wide reminder about it.
Parent, Thu: That would be great, thank you for being so understanding about all of this, and for taking the time to walk through it rather than just saying the grade stands.
Teacher, Thu (later): Grade is updated to reflect the on-time credit tier since he resubmitted within the one-week window, so this won't show as a zero or a late penalty on his report card. I'll send a class-wide reminder about hitting final submit, not just saving a draft, before next week's project is due.
Parent, Thu (later): Perfect, really appreciate you closing the loop on the grade specifically, that's the part I was most anxious about going into this. Thanks for working through it with us instead of just leaving it as a standoff.
